dedupe_keys.name: production in a circular economy nist web based idef functional model of manufacturing activities in a circular economy

description: Production in a Circular Economy is a functional model published by the US National Institute of Standards and Technology that describes, activity by activity, how manufacturing works when products and materials are kept in circulation. The archived repository read on 2026-09-28 through Software Heritage, last changed in February 2026, contains the model as a set of HTML pages with system diagrams, built with Python scripts that edit IDEF-style diagrams and served as a Jekyll website that can be hosted locally. Activity pages include acquiring materials, assembling, recapturing by-products, chemical recycling, cleaning, separating and sorting products, collecting end-of-life products and controlling equipment. Coverage is generic manufacturing, not a place. Access is free under NIST's software notice, which allows use, copying and modification provided the notice is kept. Caveats: it is a qualitative process model with no quantities or simulation, and the published website was not opened. It supports industrial and waste system planning, such as mapping where collection and recycling infrastructure plugs into a manufacturing process before building a flow or capacity model. No related circular manufacturing record is catalogued.
